summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — AMD +6%, AVGO +6%, ANET +5%, P +3%, VLO +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (GPN -12%, SMCI -11%, KDP -7%, MRNA -7%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: GPN (-12.01%) — Reuters reported PE firms CD&R and GTCR dropped early-stage take-private talks, unwinding takeover premium and merger-arb positions. Sources differ on the date (Nov 12 vs 13) but agree on the cause and size of the drop. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid/large-cap payments name, likely excluded by sector/liquidity screens). It was also a news-driven gap-down from a deal-rumor unwind, which a long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot wouldn't take.

top_movers.catalyst: William Blair upgraded AMD to Outperform on competitor shifts, with a UBS note on server CPU share and a chip rally on CoreWeave results. Reports of an Nvidia CEO exit are unverified.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AMD is a ~$585 large-cap semiconductor name that no strategy lists. The move was a same-day analyst upgrade and sector rotation, so a post-open signal would have been late and any gap filter likely capped it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap semis (AMD, AVGO, INTC) to the momentum-trader universe, and let a sector-breadth trigger (e.g. SOXX up ≥3% with ≥3 semis up ≥4%) admit them for the day.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-13; searches turned up nothing dated that day. Likely a sector-wide AI/semiconductor rally or a technical move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AVGO is a mega-cap semiconductor name that no strategy's universe includes, so no filter ever evaluated it. With no identifiable catalyst, a news-reactive strategy would have had no trigger either.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mega-cap AI/semiconductor names (AVGO, NVDA, AMD, TSM) to the momentum strategy's universe. Gate them with the existing gap and volume filters, such as ≥1.5× average volume and a ≥+3% gap, rather than loosening those filters.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-13. Searches returned nothing dated that day, so this is likely an AI-networking/semis sector move or a continuation of the AI-infrastructure rally.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. ANET is a large-cap networking/AI-infrastructure stock, and no strategy includes it, so no filter (RSI, gap, volume) was ever applied. A +5% move with no catalyst also gives a news-reactive bot no trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap AI-infrastructure names (ANET, plus peers such as AVGO and CSCO) to the momentum-trader universe. Gate entry on a ≥+3% gap or day move with ≥1.5× average volume, rather than requiring a news catalyst.

top_movers.catalyst: No dated Nov-13 news found; P is Everpure (ex-Pure Storage), in a strong AI-storage rally (+147% in 6 months, ~$3.7B backlog), so likely momentum/sector bid.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: a mid/large-cap enterprise-storage tech name that recently changed its ticker from PSTG to single-letter P. A stale symbol map likely dropped it. +3.4% with no catalyst also fails news-reactive gap filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a ticker-alias/rename check (PSTG→P) to the universe loader, and add P to the momentum universe with a 6-month return ≥ +50% and ADV ≥ $100M screen so AI-hardware leaders get included.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-13. This looks like a refiner or energy-sector move on strong refining margins, and no Valero-specific headline turned up.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. VLO is a ~$375 large-cap refiner in the energy sector, and no strategy covers it. A +3% sector-driven move with no gap or earnings trigger also wouldn't pass momentum or news-reactive filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap energy/refiners (VLO, MPC, PSX) to the momentum strategy's universe. Gate entry on sector relative strength, such as the XLE 5-day return above 0 and a volume ratio of at least 1.2×.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed Nov 13 catalyst found. Likely an energy-sector or crude-oil bounce, possibly with follow-through from Devon's Nov 5 Q3 results or an unverified Eagle Ford asset-sale report.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. DVN is a large-cap E&P, and no strategy's universe covers it, so no filter ever evaluated it. A +2.85% sector-beta move with no gap or earnings trigger would also fail momentum and news-reactive entry thresholds.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-ETF-relative screen: add large-cap energy names such as DVN to the momentum universe when XLE or XOP is up ≥1.5% and the name's volume is ≥1.2× its 20-day average. Alternatively, add an energy sleeve driven by the crude-oil move.

top_movers.catalyst: Reuters reported PE firms CD&R and GTCR dropped early-stage take-private talks, unwinding takeover premium and merger-arb positions. Sources differ on the date (Nov 12 vs 13) but agree on the cause and size of the drop.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid/large-cap payments name, likely excluded by sector/liquidity screens). It was also a news-driven gap-down from a deal-rumor unwind, which a long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot wouldn't take.
top_movers.suggestion: (No actionable change for shorts, since the bot is long-only.) For longs, add a news-reactive watchlist rule that flags M&A-rumor names. After a ≥8% gap-down on a collapsed bid, a mean-reversion entry could be considered if RSI(2) <10 and volume is ≥2× the 20-day average.

top_movers.catalyst: Reported DOJ probe into possible China diversion of Super Micro hardware, on top of margin worries after Q1 guidance (10.4–10.8% gross margin) and a month-long AI-server selloff. Sources disagree on dates and details.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SMCI is a volatile mid/large-cap AI-hardware name that no strategy lists. The drop was also a headline-driven legal shock, so a technical or momentum filter had no pre-signal and nothing to buy.
top_movers.suggestion: Add SMCI and peers (DELL, HPE) to a news-reactive watchlist, and add a regulatory-headline gate that blocks new longs for N days after a single-day drop ≥8% on DOJ/SEC keywords. A short-capable strategy would be needed to trade it.

top_movers.catalyst: Not confirmed. The likeliest driver is KDP's ~$2B common stock offering to cut debt before its Beverage Co/Global Coffee Co split. The sources conflict on the date, and none confirms the -7.4% close.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. KDP is a large-cap consumer staple that is leveraged after the JDE Peet's deal, and a dilutive offering gap is a catalyst-driven move that a momentum or mean-reversion screen wouldn't have caught.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a news-reactive rule that flags large-cap staples gapping down ≥5% on a secondary-offering or 424B5 filing. Since the bot has no short capability, treat it as an avoid-list or post-offering mean-reversion watch rather than a trade.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-13. Searches returned only older Moderna selloffs, so this is likely a sector or biotech/vaccine-policy move, or a pullback after a recent run-up.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. MRNA is a mid-cap, volatile, event-driven biotech, and no strategy lists it. With no clear catalyst, a news-reactive filter had no trigger, and a long-only bot would not short a -7% drop.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a small high-beta biotech/healthcare sleeve (for example MRNA, NVAX, BNTX) to the mean-reversion universe. Require a one-day drop of at least 6% on 1.5x average volume and no news flag before a bounce entry.
